boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Molloy ceremonies and recurring community practices, from commencement-week customs to service and cultural events.

cards.title: Convocation, the reimagined Class Night
cards.subtitle: Molloy commencement week
cards.notes: If you are graduating, register for your school’s ceremony to receive your hood and see departmental awards before commencement.
cards.short_summary: Molloy’s Class Night tradition continues as a hooding-and-awards convocation.
cards.evidence_claim: Molloy identifies Convocation as its reimagined Class Night and says the ceremony honors students with hoods and departmental awards before commencement.
cards.access_notes: For graduating students; the university page provides school-specific registration information.

cards.title: Read the colors on the fourragère
cards.subtitle: Molloy commencement ceremony
cards.notes: Look for the braided cord over graduates’ left shoulders; its white, rose, gold, and blue colors mark Dean’s List recognition.
cards.short_summary: A color-coded braided cord recognizes undergraduate Dean’s List semesters.
cards.evidence_claim: Molloy’s commencement program says its fourragère is a symbol of scholastic achievement and its colors identify the number of semesters of Dean’s List recognition.
cards.access_notes: Appears as part of commencement regalia; consult the university’s graduation communications for participation details.

cards.title: The nursing pin, designed by the first class
cards.subtitle: Barbara H. Hagan School of Nursing and Health Sciences
cards.notes: Graduating nursing students can watch for School instructions on the pinning ceremony, where pins are blessed, presented, and paired with an ethics pledge.
cards.short_summary: Nursing graduates receive a Molloy-specific pin designed by the program’s first graduating class.
cards.evidence_claim: Molloy’s report on its annual nursing pinning says the university’s nursing pin was designed by the program’s first graduating class.
cards.source_title: Molloy University Honors Nursing Graduates in Pinning Ceremony
cards.access_notes: For graduating nursing students and their invited guests; event details are issued by the School of Nursing.

cards.title: Senior Week ends at commencement
cards.subtitle: Molloy graduation season
cards.notes: Seniors should use the Student Affairs schedule to track graduation-week programming, whose documented finale is the President’s presentation of diplomas.
cards.short_summary: Molloy’s handbook frames commencement as the finale of Senior Week.
cards.evidence_claim: Molloy’s Student Handbook states that commencement, marked by the President’s presentation of diplomas, is the finale of Senior Week.
cards.access_notes: Senior Week programming is intended for graduating students; confirm current dates with Student Affairs.

cards.title: Underclassmen serve in the Honor Guard
cards.subtitle: Molloy commencement ceremony
cards.notes: Interested underclassmen can ask Student Affairs about usher or Honor Guard opportunities that support graduation ceremonies.
cards.short_summary: Molloy documents underclassmen’s role as commencement ushers or Honor Guard.
cards.evidence_claim: Molloy’s Student Handbook says underclassmen participate in commencement-related events as ushers or Honor Guard.
cards.access_notes: Participation is organized through university graduation planning; availability can vary by year.

cards.entity_name: Mary E. Lilly Club, Team and Publication Recognition Night
cards.title: Celebrate clubs at Mary E. Lilly Night
cards.subtitle: Molloy student organizations
cards.notes: Nominate and celebrate active students through your club, team, or publication when Student Affairs announces the annual recognition night.
cards.short_summary: An annual event honors people who contribute time and energy to Molloy organizations.
cards.evidence_claim: Molloy’s Student Handbook describes Mary E. Lilly Club, Team and Publication Recognition Night as an annual event honoring participation in Molloy organizations.
cards.access_notes: For participants in Molloy clubs, teams, and publications; monitor Student Affairs announcements.

cards.title: Trace the legacy of 55 Nights
cards.subtitle: Historic Molloy student tradition
cards.notes: Ask the archives or alumni office for more context on 55 Nights, a named student tradition documented in Molloy’s history of Mary E. Lilly.
cards.short_summary: A historic named tradition connected to student leader Mary E. Lilly.
cards.evidence_claim: Molloy’s Student Handbook records that Mary Elizabeth Lilly, Class of 1967, was chairman of “Sophomore Tradition and 55 Nights.”
cards.access_notes: Historic reference only; the handbook does not establish that this practice is currently offered.

cards.title: Molloy Goes Global
cards.subtitle: Molloy cultural and religious diversity celebration
cards.notes: Visit the interactive tables when the festival returns to learn through club-led games, displays, artifacts, and cultural or religious programming.
cards.short_summary: A student-founded festival creates interactive ways to share cultural and religious traditions.
cards.evidence_claim: Molloy’s DEI report says the student-founded Molloy Goes Global Cultural Festival is sponsored by Leaders for Racial Justice and Student Government.
cards.access_notes: Programming and timing vary; look for announcements from Leaders for Racial Justice and Student Government.

cards.entity_name: Molloy Martin Luther King Jr. Day of Service
cards.title: Join Molloy’s MLK Day of Service
cards.subtitle: Molloy community service tradition
cards.notes: Check university communications before January for service opportunities tied to Dr. King’s legacy and Molloy’s community-service commitment.
cards.short_summary: A recurring university service observance connected to Martin Luther King Jr. Day.
cards.evidence_claim: A Molloy presidential message states that the university would hold its seventh annual MLK Day of Service in 2025.
cards.source_title: News, Messages and Speeches | Molloy University
cards.access_notes: Activities are announced by the university; participation options and locations can vary each year.

cards.title: Night Out on the Lion
cards.subtitle: Molloy–Rockville Centre community program
cards.notes: Volunteer through athletics or campus partners when this annual family event returns; Molloy students and athletes lead games and arts-and-crafts activities.
cards.short_summary: An annual family activity night led by Molloy students and student-athletes.
cards.evidence_claim: Molloy reports that Night Out on the Lion is an annual event where Rockville Centre children take part in games and arts and crafts led by Molloy students and athletes.
cards.source_title: Communiversity Program Strengthens Ties with Molloy University and Rockville Centre
cards.access_notes: Volunteer roles and event scheduling are coordinated through the Communiversity program and athletics.
